findings.finding: Nothing invokes verify_local.py — no hook, no skill step, no workflow. It delivers a runnable pre-flight, not an automatic one, so the CI round-trip it targets is unchanged until someone types the command. Left deliberately: installing a pre-push hook changes how every push in the repo behaves and is the operator's call under --autonomous. Recorded as trg-486cb11c and stated in the module docstring, CLAUDE.md and docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md.

plan.disposition: Phase Matrix (SKILL.md section 6, NORMATIVE): External LLM Review is 'skip' at trivial and small; this run is small with risk_flags=[] (all four diff-driven detectors returned False on the real changed-file list). Not an operator decline and not a capability limit.

findings.finding: FALSE RED, repo-wide: _GUARD_SCRIPT.search searches the RAW run body, which for `run: |` blocks includes shell # comment lines. ci.yml's 'Run shared tests' carries 34 comment lines; one mentioning a checker enrols that TEST step as an unregisterable guard and fails the reverse-drift test on EVERY PR.
findings.suggestion: Strip comments before matching, mirroring test_checks_that_gate.py:69.

findings.finding: Forward-drift asserts SUBSTRING containment while verify_local.py:57 and the docs claim 'byte-identical'/'verbatim'. ci.yml growing `--strict` keeps the test green while the wrapper runs the weaker command and reports PASS on a push CI rejects.
findings.suggestion: Assert line equality.

findings.finding: Reverse-drift reads only the python-checks job. A guard added in a NEW job (then marked Required) is invisible; verify_local keeps printing full coverage.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate guard steps across ALL jobs.

findings.finding: _STDLIB_ONLY is an exact enumeration of today's imports, so any NEW stdlib import (`import os`) fails with a message blaming ADR-045 — a violation that is not there.
findings.suggestion: Use sys.stdlib_module_names.

findings.finding: The non-ASCII test asserts only the ASCII half; the arrow, the entire subject, is never asserted. Dropping encoding='utf-8' keeps it green.
findings.suggestion: Assert the non-ASCII characters survive.

findings.finding: Three-way duplication with test_checks_that_gate.py (_REQUIRED_JOB, YAML step access, a third definition of 'is this a gate step'). Re-implementing the mechanics is what produced the comment-leak bug.
findings.suggestion: Share the ci.yml step-reading helper.

findings.finding: Only two of three gates reconfigure their stdio; check_ci_gate_coverage.py prints em-dashes and does not. On Windows a child writing to a PIPE encodes with the locale codec, so a failing CI-gate guard prints mojibake. Also no timeout, unlike both neighbours (900/600).
findings.suggestion: Force the child encoding via env; add a timeout.

findings.finding: The '~5 s' cost claim is unverified locally and looks optimistic; verify_contract_surface drives grade.py over the whole monorepo.
findings.suggestion: Measure on the Windows host and quote the real number.

findings.finding: _fake keys off Path(command[2]).stem and defaults unrecognised commands to PASS, so a Gate.command shape change fails misdirected rather than at the seam.
findings.suggestion: Match against LOCAL_GATES; raise on unrecognised.

findings.finding: The file enforcing 'never bind repo modules by sys.path' loads its own subject via sys.path.append; the repo convention for this job is spec_from_file_location.
findings.suggestion: Load via spec_from_file_location.

findings.finding: echo=print is a test-only seam with one production caller; capsys already provides it.
findings.suggestion: Drop the echo parameter; assert via capsys.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: this removes the round-trip tail the docstring describes — verify_local is referenced by no hook, no SKILL.md step, no F-phase and no workflow - only prose and its own tests. The cited failures came from iterate runs, and agents execute steps, not prose. The diff ships a correct tool with no consumer.
findings.suggestion: scripts/hooks/pre-push (core.hooksPath already points there), or an F0 step guarded on the file existing

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a PASS here means CI would pass — all three gates read the working tree; a fix left unstaged is vetted locally and never pushed. Untracked test dirs cause the inverse false red.
findings.suggestion: print HEAD sha + dirty-file count; warn when dirty

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: forcing PYTHONIOENCODING makes the child readable — it does not touch locale.getpreferredencoding(); verify_contract_surface.py's two subprocess.run(..., text=True) calls have no encoding= and decode grade.py's UTF-8 stderr as cp1252 on Windows -> UnicodeDecodeError, green in CI
findings.suggestion: set PYTHONUTF8=1

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the timeout prevents an indefinite wait — subprocess.run kills only uv; on Windows it then calls communicate() with no timeout, blocking on pipes held by surviving grandchildren
findings.suggestion: Popen + communicate(timeout=) + kill the process tree

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a checker named in a comment cannot enrol a step — _run_body strips only lines whose first non-space char is '#'. A TRAILING shell comment mentioning any check_*/verify_*.py enrols that step and reddens every PR.
findings.suggestion: strip from the first whitespace-preceded '#'; add the trailing case

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the reverse-drift test catches the next guard that lands — it reads ci.yml only (7 workflows exist, 2 more Required); a workflow-call job has no steps; an unnamed step is skipped; _GUARD_SCRIPT needs a literal scripts/ segment
findings.suggestion: scan all workflows; fail loudly on a job with no steps that is not a uses: call

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the registry is self-consistent — _GUARD_SCRIPT matches scripts/verify_local.py itself. Wiring the tool into ci.yml forces registration; registering it in LOCAL_GATES makes verify() spawn itself recursively.
findings.suggestion: assert no Gate.script is verify_local.py

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: CI_ONLY_GATES records a reason, so coverage cannot silently shrink — the only assertion is len > 30, and the deferred entry cites card 'P1-b' which appears nowhere in the repo, so nothing will ever sweep it
findings.suggestion: cite a resolvable triage id; distinguish structural from deferred

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: docs point the reader at the drift contract — two citations name test_verify_local.py; both drift directions live in test_verify_local_ci_drift.py
findings.suggestion: fix both citations

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: measured 6 s on Windows — measured from inside .worktrees/<slug>, which contains no .worktrees; grade.py's walkers exclude .venv but NOT .worktrees, and CLAUDE.md documents running from the repo root
findings.suggestion: re-measure from the main clone or drop the absolute figure

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: each guard is registered exactly once — _guard_steps returns a dict keyed by step name; two jobs with the same step name silently keep the last
findings.suggestion: assert no duplicate names

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the ADR-045 test proves the checkers are never imported — ImportFrom with level > 0 is skipped and importlib.import_module is not an import node; the test proves 'no static absolute non-stdlib import'
findings.suggestion: state the scope in the docstring

external_code.disposition: Same rule: at small with no risk flags the external review pass is not triggered by the Phase Matrix. The internal cascade DID run in full (spec HARD-GATE, code, doubt) under the CLAUDE.md standing grant, and its 23 findings were addressed rather than deferred.
